scenario: Agent reads a user's inbox (gmail.readonly) and sends mail on their behalf

verdict.headline: Heavy review-gated: works in testing today, but reading mail in production needs Google verification plus an annual third-party security assessment.

your_effort.summary: Roughly 1-3 days of hands-on work to prepare (privacy policy, demo video, scope justification, consent screen), plus remediation time if the security scan finds issues.

provider_wait.summary: Plan for several weeks end to end. Sources disagree on exact numbers and Google does not commit to one.

claims.statement: Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes must complete Google's OAuth app verification before being granted access.
Apps using only non-sensitive scopes do not have to complete verification, but need lighter brand verification to show an app name and logo on the consent screen.
Apps with restricted scopes must re-verify every year.
gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, gmail.compose and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted scopes.
claims.note: Both sources are vendors. Confirm against Google's Gmail scopes page, which the console also shows automatically.

claims.statement: gmail.send is a sensitive scope, not restricted, so a send-only agent avoids the security assessment.
Restricted scopes require a CASA security assessment performed by a Google-approved assessor, in addition to verification.
claims.note: The assessor is an interested party. Google's review team contacts you when it is time to start.

claims.statement: CASA assessments are paid; third-party estimates run from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars per year.
claims.note: Single vendor estimate; assessor price lists not checked.

claims.statement: Verification for sensitive-only scopes is reported to take usually under a week.
Plan for roughly 3-8 weeks from submission to approval for restricted scopes, including the security assessment.
claims.basis: Composio quotes Google as saying restricted review can take several weeks; Nango says approval often lands in under a week and a CASA Tier 2 in about 5 days is feasible; another source says Google commits to no number. The range is a planning buffer built from these conflicting reports, not a measured figure.

claims.statement: Until verified, an app requesting sensitive or restricted scopes shows an 'unverified app' warning and is capped at 100 users.
claims.note: From a consultancy blog; confirm the cap in the Cloud Console.

claims.statement: A mismatch between scopes in your code and scopes on the consent screen forces the unverified-app screen and can stall verification.
In Testing mode, refresh tokens have a shortened lifetime, which can quietly break long-lived agent connections.
Restricted-scope review expects a privacy policy, an app demo video, and scope justifications.
claims.note: Exact required assets should be read from Google's verification requirements page.

claims.statement: Live probes of Google's discovery document and authorize endpoint were not run.
claims.what_we_tried: The research sandbox only allows a fixed list of domains and cannot reach accounts.google.com, so no probe could run. The probe runner must execute from the deployed app or a developer's machine.

claims.statement: Account creation, 2FA, and proving ownership of your app's domain must be done by a human.
claims.basis: Standard pattern for cloud consoles; no source fetched confirming the domain-ownership step for Google specifically.

claims.statement: Managed OAuth lets you skip your own verification and assessment, because they apply to the app owned by whoever holds the Google Cloud project.
claims.note: Source is a vendor of managed OAuth. Trade-offs (consent-screen branding, control, limits) not yet checked.

steps.title: Decide your scopes first
steps.detail: Send-only agents can use gmail.send (sensitive). Reading mail needs a restricted scope, which adds the security assessment.

steps.title: Create the Google Cloud project and consent screen
steps.detail: Needs your Google account, 2FA, and your app's domain.

steps.title: Add only the scopes you will really use; keep code and consent screen identical
steps.detail: Agent can diff scopes in code against the consent-screen list.

steps.title: Prepare the pre-submission kit
steps.detail: Agent drafts the privacy policy checklist, scope justification text, and demo video script.

steps.title: Submit for verification; start the security assessment when Google asks
steps.detail: Pick an approved assessor, run a first scan, fix findings.

steps.title: Put a yearly re-verification date on the calendar

blockers.do: Check that code scopes match the consent screen, and confirm whether you are past the 100-user cap while verification is pending.

blockers.if: Connections die after about a week
blockers.do: You are probably still in Testing mode; publish the app or plan for re-auth.

blockers.if: You are blocked on a restricted-scope review
blockers.do: Narrow to the fewest scopes; consider gmail.send-only, or use a managed OAuth app.

expected_vs_found.expected: All Gmail scopes are restricted and need the security audit.
expected_vs_found.found: Corrected: gmail.send is sensitive only, so send-only agents skip the audit.
Corrected: restricted scopes re-verify every year.

expected_vs_found.expected: Google publishes how long review takes.
expected_vs_found.found: Corrected: sources disagree and Google reportedly commits to no number, so we give a range with low confidence.

expected_vs_found.expected: An agent can verify the flow with live probes.
expected_vs_found.found: Not possible from the research sandbox; probes must run elsewhere.

expected_vs_found.expected: Restricted scopes need a security assessment.
expected_vs_found.found: Confirmed by multiple secondary sources; Google's own page confirms annual re-verification.
